newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bearish mood seen persisting on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Bearish mood seen persisting on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Nigerian shares will slide further before gains can be expected, dealers said on Friday after the bourse index fell below 8000 for the first time since mid-March.
The all-share index closed at 7971.84 from 8012.22 on Thursday.
Dealers blamed the trend on Nigeria's harsh economic environment. They also said difficulties with a newly introduced clearing system had not helped.
"What we are seeing is continuously depressed share prices since the end of the first quarter and nobody can say objectively when it will end," said one analyst.
However some are still hopeful that the military government's release of money to ministries will help to reflate the economy and boost company profits.
"The fund release should help improve things but I don't expect a spectacular turnaround until some time next year," said Niyi Opeodu of Leads Investments.
Leading shares which suffered on Friday include personal products giant PZ Industries the highest capitalised stock on the exchange. It fell 20 kobo to 22.80 naira.
UAC was down 39 kobo at 13.01 naira.
West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) dropped to 59.50 naira, down 35 kobo while Nigerian Breweries slid by eight kobo to 16.40 naira.
Flour Mills finished 20 kobo down at 15.40 naira and Nigerian Bottling Company at 48.50 naira closed 50 kobo lower.
African Petroleum at 48.50 naira, Agip at 13.30 naira and Unipetrol at 62.00 naira all fell 50 kobo.
Bucking the trend were some smaller banking and insurance shares.
AIICO Insurance rose 30 kobo to 17.30 naira and Prestige strengthened by 10 kobo at 6.50 naira.
Afribank climbed to 3.90 naira, up two kobo, just as International Merchant Bank which ended at 1.73 naira.
However Guaranty Trust Bank fell seven kobo to 5.05 naira and Wema Bank was down two kobo at 4.00 naira.
Paint firm IPWA was up four kobo at 2.00 naira and Franco-Nigerian trading company CFAO added 10 kobo to 3.20 naira.
